question: What are the two main components that make up the central nervous system?
explanation: The central nervous system consists exclusively of the brain and the spinal cord, which serve as the primary processing center for the body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the main job of the peripheral nervous system?

options.A: To connect the central nervous system to the rest of the body
options.C: To store long-term memories in the brain
options.D: To protect the delicate spinal cord from physical injury

explanation: You got it! Think of the peripheral nervous system as the network of highways carrying messages back and forth between your brain/spinal cord and your limbs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the name of the tough outer covering that wraps around an entire peripheral nerve?
explanation: That's correct! The epineurium is the strong outer coat that shields the nerve from everyday bumps and wear-and-tear. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h2)

question: Which tiny connective tissue layer wraps directly around a single nerve fiber?
explanation: Well done! The endoneurium is the delicate innermost layer that gives tender loving care and insulation to each individual nerve fiber. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h2)

question: How many pairs of cranial nerves emerge directly from the brain?
explanation: There are 12 pairs of cranial nerves that connect the brain directly to various structures mostly located in the head and neck. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which cranial nerve travels way past the neck to control organs in the chest and belly?
explanation: That's right! The vagus nerve is a wanderer (which is what 'vagus' means) that reaches down into the chest and abdomen to help run your internal organs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h3)

question: How many pairs of spinal nerves are connected to the human spinal cord?
explanation: The human body has 31 pairs of spinal nerves grouped by regions along the spinal column, from the neck down to the tailbone. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why does the body have nerve plexuses (networks of mixed nerves)?

options.A: To separate pain signals before they reach the brain
options.B: To make fluid that protects the spinal cord roots
options.C: To mix nerve fibers so one minor injury doesn't totally paralyze a whole limb
options.D: To create electrical sparks without the spinal cord

explanation: Great job! Plexuses act like backup generator networks, ensuring that a single injury won't knock out movement in an entire arm or leg. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which type of nerve pathway carries messages from the body up to the brain and spinal cord?
explanation: Spot on! Remember: 'A'fferent arrives at the central nervous system with sensory info from your body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the main job of sensory receptors in the peripheral nervous system?

options.A: To turn things like touch, heat, and pressure into electrical signals
options.B: To protect delicate nerve bundles from getting crushed
options.C: To release hormones that control your blood pressure
options.D: To tell your skeletal muscles to squeeze tightly

explanation: You nailed it! Sensory receptors act like translators, converting physical feelings from the environment into the electrical language your nerves understand. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the main target tissue of the somatic nervous system?
explanation: Correct! The somatic system controls your voluntary movements by talking directly to your skeletal muscles. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h6)

question: How do somatic motor pathways typically reach their target muscles?

options.A: They operate completely without you ever knowing
options.B: They use a two-neuron chain with a ganglion in the middle
options.C: They only stimulate internal glands and organs
options.D: They use a single direct neuron straight to the muscle

explanation: That's right! Somatic pathways take a straight, fast path from the spinal cord straight to the skeletal muscle with no stops in between. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which part of the nervous system kicks in during a 'fight-or-flight' stress response?
explanation: Spot on! The sympathetic system pumps up your heart rate and gets your body ready for action when you're stressed or scared. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h7)

question: A patient experiences a sudden drop in heart rate and active digestion after eating a large meal. Which system is most active?
explanation: The parasympathetic division dominates during restful states, encouraging digestion and slowing down bodily activity. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the biggest benefit of having a reflex arc that goes through the spinal cord?

options.A: It lets you consciously analyze pain before you react
options.B: It gives a super fast, automatic reaction to protect your body from harm
options.C: It stops sensory messages from ever reaching the brain
options.D: It forces your brain to think carefully before any tiny movement

explanation: Brilliant! Reflexes skip the slow brain-thinking process so you can pull your hand away from a hot stove instantly before you get badly burned. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h8)

question: Which part of a reflex arc carries the action command away from the spinal cord to the muscle?
explanation: That's correct! Efferent neurons ('E' for exit) carry the final command out from the spinal cord to tell the muscle or gland what to do. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h8)

question: Which chronic medical condition is a leading cause of peripheral neuropathy?
explanation: Long-term high blood sugar levels commonly damage peripheral nerves, making diabetes the most frequent cause of neuropathy. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h9)

question: As a nurse, what is a crucial daily check for a patient with severe nerve damage (neuropathy) in their feet?

options.A: Checking their feet every day for cuts and sores they might not feel
options.B: Soaking their feet in very hot water every night to help blood flow
options.C: Encouraging them to walk barefoot inside to toughen the skin
options.D: Applying strong chemical creams to permanently numb the skin

explanation: You nailed this nursing priority! Because neuropathy patients can't feel pain well, daily foot checks stop small cuts from turning into major, infected ulcers. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h9)
